verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only objection raised, maintenance-fit-1, was refuted because it depends on a future pg_hosts.conf format change that the thread mentions only as an idea. The view copies the shipped pg_hba_file_rules design, and the thread settled the rule_number column and the behaviour on builds without SNI. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and only 3 of 9 messages are shown.

brief.title: Add pg_hosts_file_rules view to inspect pg_hosts.conf
brief.problem: Postgres has pg_hba_file_rules for pg_hba.conf but no matching view for pg_hosts.conf, the hosts configuration file that maps SNI host names to SSL certificate settings. The author noticed the gap while working on a configuration file format proposal. Administrators cannot check from SQL whether the current file parses.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds a set-returning function and a system view over it, built the same way as pg_hba_file_rules. The view parses the current file on disk, not what the server last loaded, and shows one row per entry with an error column for bad lines. On builds without SNI support, such as LibreSSL, the file is not parsed and the view is always empty.
user_visible_surface: New system view pg_hosts_file_rules, readable only by superusers by default.
New function pg_hosts_file_rules() in pg_proc, used by the view definition.
View columns: file_name, line_number, hostnames text[], ssl_certificate, ssl_key, ssl_ca, passphrase_command, passphrase_command_reload, error.
The rule_number column from v1 was dropped in later versions because pg_hosts.conf is unordered.
author_claims: The view gives pg_hosts.conf the same inspection tool that pg_hba_file_rules gives pg_hba.conf.
Users can check planned file changes before a reload, or diagnose a failed load.
Leaving the view empty on builds without SNI avoids telling users a file is valid when SNI cannot work.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson supported the idea, reviewed several versions, and called it nearly ready for v20 after two nits, which v4 addressed. solai v tested v3 without issues; v5 fixed an EXEC_BACKEND test failure and no one has replied since.
unclear: The material does not say whether the function itself is executable by non-superusers or only the view is restricted.
The docs do not say whether included files, if pg_hosts.conf supports them, appear with their own file_name.
No one discussed whether passphrase_command values should be visible, since they may expose secret-related commands.
The material does not say how the view handles a missing pg_hosts.conf, though a test for it was requested.

Stephen Frost shared the concern about splitting up keywords and asked for a lookup function as well. prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 showed the loaded pg_hba.conf, and reviewers found its mapping of keywords and options onto columns confusing. pg_hosts.conf entries are flat and unordered, and this view parses the file on disk as pg_hba_file_rules does.

refuted.title: Fixed per-setting columns while the pg_hosts.conf format may grow
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new per-host setting to pg_hosts.conf, for example from the configuration rework. The parser accepts it but the view has no column for it, and no test fails. Users who check the file with the view do not see the new setting, and each such addition changes the view's shape and rules.out.
refuted.argument: The view gives each pg_hosts.conf field its own column, while pg_hba_file_rules puts open-ended settings in an options text[] column. In message #3 the author says the config rework is already considering "what else could be in pg_hosts", so the format is likely to grow soon. Once released, the view's column set is a user-facing interface that later format changes must keep compatible or break.
refuted.author_must_show: How will the view handle new pg_hosts.conf settings from the planned rework, and should certificate options go into an options column like pg_hba_file_rules?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future format change that the material only mentions as an idea in message #3. The documented columns map one to one to today's entries, as the fixed columns of pg_hba_file_rules do, and Postgres adds system view columns in major releases routinely.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a pg_proc.dat entry and a system view in system_views.sql, so it needs a catversion bump.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes src/include/libpq/hba.h, a header that extensions can include.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The view shows ssl_key paths and passphrase_command text, and is readable only by superusers by default.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The view has one column per pg_hosts.conf field, so a new field in the file needs a new column.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does system_views.sql revoke EXECUTE on pg_hosts_file_rules() from public, as it does for pg_hba_file_rules()?
Should the docs warn that granting SELECT on the view exposes passphrase_command text and private key paths?
What does the view return when pg_hosts.conf is missing: no rows, an error row, or a thrown error?
If pg_hosts.conf supports include directives, do entries from included files appear with their own file_name and line_number?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson supported the idea in message #2 and reviewed several versions; the owner needs to know the SSL and SNI code and the hba file parsing code.
committability.liability: One superuser-only view and function whose columns must follow the pg_hosts.conf format in every later release, plus the rule that the view stays empty on builds without SNI.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted five versions in response to review and moved the entry to the next CommitFest, and v5 fixed an EXEC_BACKEND test failure.

priority.reason: The patch is about 21 KB, touches eight files and reuses the pg_hba_file_rules mechanism in hbafuncs.c. Only administrators who use SNI with pg_hosts.conf benefit, the cost falls only on people who query the view, and v5 has no reply yet.

provisional_note: Without the code, the privileges on the function, the handling of a missing or included file, and the parser changes in be-secure-common.c could not be checked. Messages #4 to #9 were not shown, so the brief's summary of them is taken as given.

precedents_retrieved.title: catalog view to pg_hba.conf file
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a system view (pg_hba_settings, later renamed pg_hba_conf) that exposes the parsed, currently loaded pg_hba.conf rules to superusers through SQL, with columns for connection type, databases, users, address/mask, auth method and options. Later versions reloaded pg_hba in backends on SIGHUP, used a materialized tuplestore, and split special keywords (all, sameuser, +role) into separate columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers were unconvinced that the mapping of pg_hba.conf onto a table was right: Peter Eisentraut found the keyword columns, compare_method and options representation confusing and questioned why a processed view was better than the raw file if it could not answer "what auth method applies to user X from address Y". Stephen Frost shared the concern about splitting up keywords and asked for a lookup function as well. The author agreed to rework the view and add such a function for 9.6, but no new patch arrived in the July commitfest, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Ultimately, I don't see how this is better than just showing the raw
file.  I don't see a sensible way to compute answers to questions such
as "What is the authentication method for user X from IP address Y.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add inline comments to the pg_hba_file_rules view
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Daniel Gustafsson, Greg Sabino Mullane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a "comment" column to the pg_hba_file_rules view that shows the end-of-line comment of each valid pg_hba.conf entry. The author wanted this so annotations such as tags or client names on hba entries can be read through SQL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that end-of-line comments are only one of several comment styles, so showing only them is incomplete, and that users may not want file comments exposed through a view. Daniel Gustafsson and Greg Sabino Mullane agreed. Daniel proposed agreeing on a separate annotation syntax for pg_hba.conf in a new thread, and the author withdrew the patch to start that discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we should leave file comments be file comments.  If we want some annotations to be exported to higher-level views, we should make that an intentional and explicit separate feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Document hostssl related concepts better
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch rewrote the hostssl material to cut repetition, mainly in the overview section, which repeated itself. It also touched how the related options are presented in the reference section.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer responded in about a year, including after the author asked for opinions in April 2024. The author withdrew the patch in February 2025 because it no longer applied after recent changes and no one had argued for or against it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Withdrawn as this now has conflicts from recent changes and no one seems
interested in voicing an opinion on this for or against.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sample configuration files
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Tom Lane, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds annotated sample configuration files for contrib modules to the source tree, listing each module's parameters and defaults. It did not install them; users would copy the values or load them with an include directive in postgresql.conf.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers doubted the files were useful, since they do nothing unless included in postgresql.conf, and setting a parameter directly or with ALTER SYSTEM SET is simpler. Tom Lane suggested a standard parameter section in each contrib module's SGML documentation instead. Votes ended about even, with no consensus for the patch, and Michael Paquier returned it as the commitfest closed; a postgresql.conf.d include directory was floated as a better direction.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This is a documentation effort
mainly, and installing those files has zero effect if they are not
loaded via include_if_exists or include in postgresql.conf.

precedents_retrieved.title: Configurable file mode mask
precedents_retrieved.authors: Stephen Frost (sfrost), Adam Brightwell (abrightwell), David Steele (dsteele)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an initdb option (-u/--file-mode-mask) and a GUC file_mode_mask so that files and directories in $PGDATA can be created with a mode other than 0077, for example group-readable. The goal is to let an unprivileged user in the postgres group run a file-level backup, and the patch also refactors BasicOpenFile(), OpenTransientFile() and PathNameOpenFile() to use a default mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew it to rework the design. Tom Lane questioned the safety of loosening the 0600 assumptions, such as the postmaster.pid and lock file checks, and asked for a flag that allows group access instead of a free umask, with no GUC that can disagree with initdb; Robert Haas also favored a group-read flag. Moving to that design, possibly taking permissions from the $PGDATA directory, made the patch too large to finish for v10.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In any case, the changes required have enlarged the size and scope of the patch considerably and we are not confident that it will be done in time to commit for v10.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_file_settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a system view, first named pg_hba_file_settings and later pg_hba_rules, that shows each line of pg_hba.conf with any parse error, similar to pg_file_settings. It lets users check pg_hba.conf before a reload and shows each rule's options in a jsonb column, built with new helper functions such as push_jsonb_string_value().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier moved it to the next CF with no reviews, then marked it returned with feedback. He questioned the use of jsonb for the options column, since the options are not nested and a simple name=value array would do. Vitaly Burovoy argued for jsonb to make filtering easier, but the thread ended without a revised patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If they were nested I'd see a case for it but it
seems to me that as presented this is just an overkill. In short, I
think that this patch needs a bit of rework, so I am marking it as
returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Configurable location for extension .control files
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started with a request to make the directory that holds extension .control files configurable, so isolated package layouts such as NixOS can install extensions outside SHAREDIR/extension. A 2015 patch added an extension_directory setting that superusers can change at runtime, mainly so extension authors can test their .control files in a local cluster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected in 2013 that the path should not be adjustable at runtime because of security concerns. In review, Heikki Linnakangas said tests also need dynamic_library_path changed, and other share data such as timezone and tsearch files is not covered. He proposed that pgxs build a temporary installation so "make check" works for extensions, and the entry was returned with feedback in that direction.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In summary, the goal is to make "make check" to work for extensions, and the way to do that is to teach pgxs to create a temporary installation.

precedents_retrieved.title: hostorder and failover_timeout for libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two libpq connection parameters. `hostorder` (sequential or random) sets the order in which the hosts in a multi-host connection string are tried, and `failover_timeout` makes libpq loop over the hosts until one connects or the timeout expires.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying, and the author did not rebase it or split it into separate `hostorder` and `failover_timeout` patches as Michael Paquier asked. Michael Paquier also doubted that a random mode alone justifies reworking libpq, and suggested that applications build their own connection strings. Tom Lane objected that the patch uses terms different from pgJDBC for nearly the same feature and overlaps two other patch threads, and these points were not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As this hasn't been done, and Tom's questions haven't been addressed,
I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

roaster_notes.note: P1 and P6 were earlier pg_hba attempts at a file-inspection view. Their recorded reasons were a jsonb options column and a confusing mapping of hba keywords to columns, and neither applies to the flat, unordered pg_hosts.conf. The view copies the shipped pg_hba_file_rules design, the thread (messages #2, #4, #7) settled the rule_number and LibreSSL questions, and P2 concerns file comments, which this proposal does not expose.

The view copies pg_hba_file_rules and pg_ident_file_mappings in naming, superuser-only default, error column and on-disk parsing, so it follows existing practice and changes nothing for existing users. The thread settled the empty result on builds without SNI and the dropped rule_number column (messages #2-#4). Fixed per-setting columns may need changes if the config rework adds pg_hosts.conf options, but changing system view columns between major versions is normal. Without the code, I could not check how a missing file or include files appear.

The proposal holds no persistent or cross-node state. It adds one pg_proc entry and one system view, both created by initdb and never dumped by pg_dump or carried over by pg_upgrade, and there is no WAL, on-disk format, wire protocol or replication change. A standby reads its own local pg_hosts.conf the same way pg_hba_file_rules reads pg_hba.conf, and the hba.h change targets a new major version only.

No security objection. The view is superuser-only by default, like pg_hba_file_rules, and a superuser can already read pg_hosts.conf and its passphrase settings. The code is not shown, so two points stay unchecked: whether system_views.sql revokes EXECUTE on pg_hosts_file_rules() from public, and whether the docs warn that granting the view exposes passphrase_command text.

Apart from this point, the design follows pg_hba_file_rules and pg_ident_file_mappings. It adds no hot-path cost and no new dependency, and a committer who knows the area (message #2, #7) is engaged. So the maintenance and fit case against it is weak.

No existing feature gives this result. pg_read_file() returns the raw pg_hosts.conf text but does not run the server's parser, and a reload applies changes instead of checking them first. The patch reuses the pg_hba_file_rules mechanism in hbafuncs.c, so it extends an existing one. An extension would have to duplicate the core parser.

I have no demand objection. The material shows no field reports, but the view copies pg_hba_file_rules and pg_ident_file_mappings for a sibling configuration file, and a committer who knows the area (message #2, #7) supports it. The cost is one superuser-only view and function, paid only by people who query it.
